mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past six months signals an easing monetary policy cycle, which reduces discount rates applied to equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05 in a t-test) despite a sustained decline in FEDFUNDS below its 2007-2008 average of 4.0% over the past six months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly drop in the unemployment rate below 3.5% triggers a surge in consumer demand and corporate investment, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% in the next month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) despite UNRATE crossing below 3.5%, or the rate does not cross the threshold within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indices signals robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next quarter (60 trading days).
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and INDPRO both increase in the same month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when both proxies rise, or their correlation is below 0.7 over the period.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), rising interest rates compress equity valuations, generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% in the current regime
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS remaining above 4.5% in the tightening regime, or the regime is not confirmed by other indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in demand (HOUST) and decline in federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) signal accommodative monetary policy, boosting equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases while FEDFUNDS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when both proxies move in opposite directions, or their correlation is below 0.6.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in demand (GDPC1) above 22,000 billions of chained 2017 dollars signals robust economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 crosses above 22,000 in the next month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite GDPC1 exceeding 22,000, or the increase is not sustained.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in the unemployment rate below 3.5% during a late-cycle expansion signals labor market strength, prompting increased consumer spending and corporate investment, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.5% in the next month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05) despite UNRATE crossing below 3.5%, or the regime is not confirmed by other indicators like GDP growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the CPIAUCSL index signals accelerating demand and price pressures, which drive positive S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05) despite a sustained upward trend in CPIAUCSL, or the inflation rate does not correlate with equity performance.
